topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing for the lecture series, outlining course objectives, student backgrounds, and core learning goals.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer and experimental model systems
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a multistep process driven by genetic alterations and disrupted tissue differentiation, and discuss experimental approaches used to model tumor biology.

topics.label: Mechanisms and pathology of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the pathological processes, histological features, and clinical distinctions between benign lesions and invasive, metastatic malignancies.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and clinical pathophysiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the systematic naming conventions for tumors and explain the mechanical and physiological mechanisms by which benign and malignant growths cause illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer epidemiology and comparative oncology across taxa
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare patterns of cancer incidence and tissue susceptibility in humans with those observed across companion animals and other multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical symptoms and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the clinical detection of tumors and evaluate the principles, histological diagnostic criteria, and utility of screening programs across various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding administrative remarks and instructions for upcoming practical sessions and lectures.
